token.name: Orsa's Knotted Toll Rope
token.description: The knots mark stretches of road where Orsa charged a toll. The last is worn flat by a thumb.

successor.name: Benna Quillon
successor.story: Grew up minding her aunt's rope on the Hub road and learned the toll trade before she could count. She moved the rope a mile east the week Orsa fell and went on charging the caravans.

token.name: Dray's Dented Pay Chit
token.description: A punched brass chit from Dray's company. Someone struck out the promised pay and wrote in a smaller sum.

successor.name: Coll Varrick
successor.story: A deserter from the United Cities' samurai who sold Dray his sword for a share. He kept the company's books, so the men followed the man who knew where the money was.

token.name: Morrow's Mended Prayer Cord
token.description: A prayer cord mended with common thread. The cut end still carries the wax of an old seal.

successor.name: Tobin Ashe
successor.story: A former Holy Nation acolyte who ran away with Morrow rather than face the Inquisition. He still prays every morning, though he no longer says to whom.

token.name: Ashvael's Tin Ration Tag
token.description: A ration tag stamped with a bowl. Ashvael scraped the issuing mark off and kept the piece.

successor.name: Gristle Mott
successor.story: Fed Ashvael's starving band for years on whatever the roads gave up. When the leader was gone, the hungry went with the one who held the pot.

token.name: Harrow's Iron Ledger Clasp
token.description: A clasp from Harrow's chain ledger. Scratches on the back mark lots sent down the road.

successor.name: Sella Harrow
successor.story: Ran the ledgers and the buyers while her husband ran the chains. Most of his old clients never noticed the change in management.

token.name: Vahl's Cracked Horn Ring
token.description: A ring cut from a broken horn. Borun left the crack where it opened in the fight.

successor.name: Ruk Vahl
successor.story: Borun's younger brother, quieter and worse. He fought his way to the front of the berserkers inside a day.

token.name: Hearthmourn's Well Stone
token.description: A smooth stone drilled for a cord. Hearthmourn carried it between the wells where she preached.

successor.name: Brother Caddoc
successor.story: Hearthmourn's first convert, a farmhand who heard her preach at a well and walked off his master's field that night. He preaches her words badly but loudly.

token.name: Crake's Snare Toggle
token.description: A bone toggle from one of Crake's snares. The grooves are cut to hold the line without a knot.

successor.name: Wenna Crake
successor.story: Raised in her father's hunting camps on the edge of the Cannibal Plains. She reads tracks better than he did and takes fewer prisoners.

token.name: Sillery's Cache Marker
token.description: A scrap of metal with a crooked arrow. Sillery kept it tied away from the maps he sold.

successor.name: Doss Kettering
successor.story: Sillery's digging partner for ten years and the only one who knew where the good caches were buried. He's been digging them up one by one ever since.

token.name: Teshin's Practice Guard
token.description: A guard off an old practice sword. There are more marks on the inside than on the edge.

successor.name: Aiko Ro
successor.story: Teshin's only student, who learned the sword by losing to him every day for four years. She took his blade from the grave and his reputation from the road.

token.name: Gorehollow's Pit Cord
token.description: A short cord doubled through two teeth. Gorehollow kept a long knot at one end for a second hand.

successor.name: Marrow Jess
successor.story: Swore blood-sisterhood with Gorehollow in a cannibal pit they both climbed out of. The raiders say she's the reason Ysolde ever came back from a fight.

token.name: Cull's Crew Tally
token.description: A crew tally cut from water-dark wood. The names change where the oldest marks were scraped away.

successor.name: Fenn Cull
successor.story: Born on one of his mother's ships and never set foot in a town until he was twelve. He runs the crew like she did, only younger and with less patience.

token.name: Clackjaw's Split Pincer
token.description: A crab pincer broken across the joint. Clackjaw bound the halves together with copper wire.

successor.name: Snapper Dunne
successor.story: The loudest of Clackjaw's raiders and the first one up the beach every time. He took over by shouting longer than anyone else.

token.name: Maruka's Shield Rivet
token.description: A flattened rivet from Maruka's shield. The rim still carries paint where the blows missed it.

successor.name: Oshar Tal-Khesh
successor.story: Carried Maruka's shield for six years and her name since she fell. The exiles follow him because he never once dropped it.

token.name: Peel's Skinning Hook
token.description: A little hook honed on both sides. Peel kept the handle wrapped in cloth for grip.

successor.name: Merrin Stitch
successor.story: Peel took him off a slaver's cart as a boy and taught him the needle instead of the knife. He finished his master's last coat himself.

token.name: Tuppence's Two-Cat Counter
token.description: A mundane brass counter stamped twice. Tuppence used it to mark a ledger that never quite balanced.

successor.name: Mister Ha'penny
successor.relation: the bones he built to follow him
successor.story: A skeleton Tuppence built from scavenged parts to carry his loot. Nobody told it to stop when its maker fell, so it picked up the ledger and carried on.

token.name: Ulla's Split Reed
token.description: A reed bound with thread at the root. The split opens when the reed is held back to the light.

successor.name: Keening Bel
successor.story: The shrieker whose voice carries furthest in the forest. Ulla's band follows the sound now, the way they used to follow Ulla.

token.name: Quell's Swamp Toll Tag
token.description: A waxed wooden toll tag. Some marks are set deeper where a village paid twice.

successor.name: Sabre Hollis
successor.story: Quell's tax collector, who knew every village in the swamp and what each one could pay. The Red Sabres decided he was too useful to lose.

token.name: Gammer's Bent Sickle Tip
token.description: A snapped sickle tip worn into a smooth curve. It still carries a little earth in the socket.

successor.name: Nan Tuck
successor.story: Gammer's wife, who planned most of the farm raids from their kitchen table while he took the credit. She doesn't bother hiding it now.

token.name: Sayo's Worn Grey Ribbon
token.description: A grey ribbon faded almost white at the fold. Sayo kept the same knot until it wore through.

successor.name: Kiri of the Torn Ribbon
successor.story: Sayo's last pupil, who tore her own grey ribbon in half the day her teacher was taken. She still takes work from the people who used to hire Sayo.

token.name: Cuddy's Floodline Marker
token.description: A section of marker shaved off above the last flood line. The lower edge is soft from standing in water.

successor.name: Little Pell
successor.story: Nobody's sure if he's Cuddy's son, his brother or just someone who started dressing like him. The flooded coast doesn't seem to care which.

token.name: Tchik's Seven-Notch Pendant
token.description: Seven shallow notches run across the face. Three have gone smooth where Tchik held the pendant.

successor.name: Tchak of Three Voices
successor.story: A drone that followed Tchik out of the hive and learned to speak in his manner. It hasn't learned all seven voices yet, but the band follows the three it has.

token.name: Vosk's Brass Contract Pin
token.description: A contract pin with a plain head. Vosk threaded it through the folded corner of his agreements.

successor.name: Garrow Vosk
successor.story: Elric's cousin, who joined the company to pay off a debt and stayed because the pay was better than farming. He takes the contracts Elric used to take, for a little less.

token.name: Ludlow's Chain Wedge
token.description: A short wedge made from a broken link. Its working edge shows where someone kept driving it under a catch.

successor.name: Esme Ludlow
successor.story: Pyke's sister, who handled the freed slaves while he handled the slavers. She still hits the caravans, and the Anti-Slavers still pretend not to know her.

offer: A woman strings a rope across the Hub road and calls it a toll. Orsa Quillon. Three caravans have stopped paying her with their lives.
Orsa Quillon, the Toll-Widow. She works the dry road out of the Hub and the hills beyond. The Guild would like the rope cut.
Merchants keep paying a woman called Quillon to cross open desert. The ones who refuse are not seen again. End it.
accept: Where on the road does she stand?
accepted: Take guards. She is rarely alone, and she never moves her rope.
Watch the hills past the Hub. She likes a crest to see you coming.
report: Quillon is dead? Then the road is open again. The Guild pays what it promised.
Her rope is cut. Good. Here is the Guild's coin.
Dead at her own toll post, they tell me. Take your cats.

offer: Ferrant Dray was a lordling with a title, an estate and debts. Now he is a highwayman with a title and a sword. The Cities want the title removed, along with the head.
Dray. Third son of a failed house, dressed like a lord and robbing like a dog. He haunts the northern flats and the green edges. Bring him down.
A so-called Lord Dray holds court over travellers in the northern flats. Tolls, taxes, a fee for being looked at. The Cities pay for his absence.
accept: A fallen noble. How hard can it be?
accepted: He keeps hired swords near him. And he fights better than he governs. Be careful.
Look in the green edges and along the flats. He avoids the Holy roads.
decline: Nobles are trouble even when ruined.
report: Dray is finished? His family will pretend they never knew him. The Cities will not. Take this.
No more Lord Dray. Good. Here is the reward.
A lordling less. I wouldn't call it a tragedy. Your cats.

offer: A deserter named Hask Morrow walked off his post with his armour and his orders. He now plunders pilgrims on the roads. The Nation wants an example made.
Sentinel Morrow broke his oath, brother. He is somewhere in Okran's Pride, robbing the faithful on their way to prayer. Return him to the Flame.
There is no pardon for a deserter who preys on pilgrims. His name is Morrow. The Holy Nation pays for the correction.
accepted: He knows our patrol routes. Do not be where he expects you.
He keeps to the green roads, near where pilgrims walk. Do not hesitate.
report: Morrow is dead? Okran's mercy is thin, but it reached him. Here is your reward.
The deserter is gone. The faithful sleep a little easier. Take this.
Done, and done properly. The Nation remembers its debts.

offer: A starving man named Sarn Ashvael preaches that the Empty Bowl will take what the road owes. His mob follows him. Starving men with a prophet are worse than starving men alone.
Ashvael. They call him a prophet of hunger. His following has grown to a mob. The Guild would rather see it starve properly.
A bandit leader named Sarn has convinced two dozen hungry wretches they are chosen. The roads in the east can't bear it. End it.
accept: Hunger has a preacher? Fine, I'll silence him.
accepted: He and his mob walk the desert and the bone edge. They'll fall on anything that looks fed.
They sing before they attack. Listen for it.
decline: I feel for them. Not today.
Find someone with a harder heart.
report: Ashvael is dead. The mob will scatter. Gods help whoever finds them first. Your reward.
A prophet less. The desert will hold its tongue for a while. Take the cats.
Hunger has lost its voice. I'm sorry for it. I'll still pay you.

offer: Veldt Harrow was a slaver. A legal one, if you like. Then the markets thinned and he stopped selling and started burying. They call him the Tallyman. He counts every head he keeps.
Harrow. He used to take people to market. Now he takes them to the ground, and he writes the numbers in a book. We want the book and the man.
A butcher walks the flood roads with a ledger. Harrow. Every caravan he stops, he marks. Do not carry that mark home.
accepted: He keeps slave hunters with him, men who still think of themselves as honest. They are not.
Look along the flood roads and the desert south of them. He prefers wet ground, for the digging.
report: Harrow is dead? Then the ledger ends. The Anti-Slavers pay. For the names in it, and for all of them.
The Tallyman has stopped counting. Good. Take this.
I won't ask how. Here is your pay.

offer: Borun Vahl, the Oathless. He broke his vow in the stone circle and was cast out. He kills those who cross his path, and calls it honour.
A Shek who lost his name hunts the high stones. Vahl. The Kingdom does not wish his story told. We wish his bones in the sand.
Vahl was a warrior until he betrayed his duel. Now he challenges travellers, and does not honour the loser. End him, flatskin.
accept: I will find him in the stones.
accepted: He fights without mercy. Do not offer a duel. Do not trust his word.
Look in the dry mountains and the canyons. He sleeps among the stones where nobody asks him questions.
report: Vahl is dead? The Stone Golem weighs all things, and tonight the scales are even. Take your reward.
The Oathless has fallen. His shame can end. Here is the pay.
You fought a Shek and lived. That is a rare thing. Take this.

offer: Ilsa Hearthmourn was a Pacifier of the Flame. She stopped believing and began to pray for the end of Okran. The heresy is spreading. She is spreading it.
The Candle Heretic. Ilsa Hearthmourn. She walks the Holy roads with a lit candle and no scripture, and the faithful follow her. She must be silenced.
An apostate. A former Pacifier. She speaks against the Flame and the people listen. The Nation will pay for her end.
accept: The Flame will judge her through me.
accepted: She keeps her old armour and her old skills. Do not trust her prayers.
Look in the Holy lands, and the hills where the faithful are scarce. She lights a candle at every camp.
decline: I will not raise a hand to pray.
I lack the faith for it.
report: Hearthmourn is dead. May the Flame forgive her, since I cannot. Here is the Nation's payment.
The Candle is out. Good. Your reward.
A heretic silenced. The faithful will breathe easier tonight.

offer: Hodd Crake was one of ours. A hunter of the plains. Somewhere out there, he started eating what he killed. He still wears the colours. That shames every hunter alive.
Crake. Fifteen years killing cannibals and then he joined them. He is not hungry, they say. He just likes the taste. Put him down.
We called him the Long Appetite. A hunter who crossed. We hunt cannibals, traveller. We do not hunt our own, unless we must. We must.
accepted: He knows our tricks. He taught half of them. Stay out of the open ground.
Crake roams the bone plains and the badlands. Look for what he leaves behind.
report: Crake is dead? He deserved a better end, and a worse life. Here is the Bastion's pay.
The Long Appetite is finished. May the hunt forgive him. Take this.
Good. We will bury the colours with him. Your cats.

offer: Pim Sillery was one of us until the day he walked out of a ruin with every schematic and left three hunters in the dark. He calls himself the Magpie. He likes shiny things.
We had a salvage crew in the ruins. Sillery looted them while they slept, and sold the plans. Bring him in, or bring the plans back. I prefer both.
The Magpie. Pim Sillery. He lives on stolen finds. Our ruins are drying up because of him. Stop him, and I will make it worth your while.
accept: A thief with a taste for tech. Fine.
accepted: He prowls the ruined fields and the old robot yards. He works with thieves who like his luck.
Be quick. He runs on a shiny trinket and a bad conscience.
report: The Magpie is dead? Good riddance. The ruins are ours again. Take your payment.
Sillery is done. We'll find his nest soon enough. Here is your fee.
A fine job. And without a single scratch on the good gear. Take the cats.

offer: Teshin Ro. A ronin. His lord died, and he has been paying for it ever since. He duels travellers and cuts the ones who refuse. Many dead, last season.
A masterless swordsman works the northern roads. Teshin Ro. He does not rob. He only challenges. And he does not leave.
The ronin Ro has killed eleven men in duels that were not duels. Someone with a good blade and a clear head should end it. The Cities pay.
accept: A ronin. Honour or no honour, I'll end it.
accepted: He fights without anger, which is worse. Watch his shoulders. They speak before the sword.
He keeps to the flats and the desert. When the wind drops, he will find you.
report: Ro has fallen? Strange. I expected a different ending. Take your pay.
The ronin is gone. May his lord forgive him. Here is the Cities' reward.
Done. And with respect, I hope. Take this.

offer: Ysolde Gorehollow. The Bloodmother. She drains prisoners into jars and sells the contents to anyone sick enough to buy. Her raiders worship it. The Cities want the jars broken.
A blood-raider matriarch works the ashlands. Gorehollow. She takes the living and returns them empty. Find her and end it.
Gorehollow runs a nest in the ash country. Her kills are hung to drain. Her cooks are patient. Do us all a favour.
accepted: She keeps a crowd of raiders about her. They love her more than their lives. Plan accordingly.
The ash country near the old domes. Follow the flies.
decline: I have no stomach for it.
report: Gorehollow is dead. The ash will be quiet. Take the Cities' payment.
The Bloodmother is gone. Good. Your reward.
I won't ask what you saw. Your cats.

offer: Marta Cull, the Brine-Wife. She ties salvagers to the tide line and times their drowning. The Guild's coastal runs are dry because of her. Make the sea quiet.
A Reaver woman holds the southern shore. Cull. She takes the cargo, and she takes the crew, and she takes her time. The Guild pays well for her silence.
Cull is a salvage queen with a drowning habit. The Guild lost nine hands to her last season. We want the ninth to be the last.
accepted: She keeps young Reavers about her. They obey and do not ask. Watch the beaches.
Look along the south coast and the old pits. Her camp stinks of fish and fear.
report: Cull is dead? Then the coast is ours again. Here is the Guild's reward.
The Brine-Wife has drowned herself. Funny. Take the cats.
A good day. Here is your pay.

offer: Teodric Clackjaw. He fought in the crab pits until he cut an opponent in half after the bell. Banned, he took a shell for armour and a grudge for a god. The Guild wants him quiet.
A crab champion gone rogue works the south. Clackjaw. He clacks his teeth before he kills, and that is the only warning you get.
Clackjaw. Disgraced in the tournaments, loose on the roads. He still insists on fighting by the rules. Only his rules. Take him out.
accepted: He and his crabbers wander the pits and the maze. Listen for the clacking.
He fights in rounds. Do not agree to a round. There is only one.
report: Clackjaw is dead? The pits will sleep easier. Here is your Guild fee.
No more clacking. A relief. Take your pay.
Good work. The Guild remembers. Your cats.

offer: Maruka Tal-Khesh calls herself the Hundred Cuts. She tests every wanderer with a blade, and counts. Few reach ten. The Kingdom does not approve of her excess.
Maruka walks the stone roads, a zealot of Kral. She believes a proper death takes a hundred cuts. She is eager to prove it. End her.
The Hundred Cuts. Maruka. Even Kral's own Chosen shy from her. Put the blade down, and take her with it.
accepted: She fights with devotion, and devotion does not tire. Watch the third cut. She prefers the third.
Look in the stone roads and the canyons. She is always where the sun is hardest.
decline: Her god is no concern of mine.
report: Maruka has fallen. Let her count her hundred in the stone halls. Your reward.
The Hundred Cuts is done. Not even Kral would call it dishonour. Take your pay.
A hard death for a hard woman. Here is the Kingdom's coin.

offer: Aldous Peel is a skinner in a coat of skins. He takes the living and strips them whole, and wears the work. Some call him the Tailor. The Nation calls him an abomination. I call him a client for you.
A skin bandit tailor works the ashlands. Peel. His coat is made of faces, and he has room for more. The Nation will pay for the coat to be burned.
Peel. A skinner. A thing without a heart who makes clothes of the ones who have. The Holy Nation wants him ended.
accepted: He moves in the ash with his tailors. You will see them before you see him. They are very neat.
The ashlands. Follow the quiet. Birds stop first.
decline: I would rather not meet him.
report: Peel is destroyed. The coat is ash? Good. The Nation pays, gladly. Take this.
The Tailor has been cut off at the thread. Your reward.
May his skins rest. Here is your pay.

offer: Mister Tuppence is a Skeleton who sells road protection. Pay him a fee, and he will not break your cart. Do not pay, and he breaks your cart, and you. It is quite orderly.
A Skeleton with a ledger and a hat. Tuppence. Charges a penny, he says, but means a great deal more. The Guild would like the ledger closed.
Tuppence. A bandit with a head for business. He has protected forty caravans and killed six. The Guild wishes the arrangement cancelled.
accepted: He is very polite, and very armed. He will offer you a receipt. Do not sign.
He works the pits and the old robot yards. Listen for the little bell.
decline: I cannot take a Skeleton seriously.
report: Tuppence is scrap? Remarkable. The Guild is relieved. Here is your fee.
The arrangement is void. Your reward.
No more protection fees. The roads will be crooked again. Take the cats.

offer: Ulla Weeper leads the shriekers. She was a mother once, they say, before the swamp took the rest. Now she screams and her followers scream with her, and anything that hears it dies.
The swamp has a woman who sings with a scream. Ulla Weeper. Her mob follows the sound. Silence her, and the swamp will be a little less terrible.
A shrieker queen. That is what the Swampers call her. Ulla. She is quiet only when she is killing. Be quick.
accepted: Stop your ears if you can. Her mob will come out of the mud before you see them.
She works the wet lands and the mud pools. If the frogs go quiet, she is near.
report: Ulla is dead? The swamp is still. I was not sure I would ever hear that. Here is your pay.
The shriekers have lost their mother. May the quiet last. Take this.
A hard job done. Here is the pay.

offer: Dunmar Quell calls himself the Red Captain. He has taken over the Red Sabres and means to rule the swamp. Every town in the wet lands pays him now, or does not pay anything again.
Quell. Too ambitious by half. He took the Sabres, and now he wants the swamp. We want him in the mud.
A boss named Dunmar Quell is making trouble in the wet. He taxes caravans, burns refusers, and calls it a kingdom. Cut it down.
accepted: His Sabres are loyal, which is rare in a bandit. Be ready for them.
Look in the swamp and along the mud pools. He rides out with his best, and returns with their spoils.
report: Quell is dead? The swamp is relieved. Here is the Swampers' pay.
The Red Captain has lost his crown. Take your reward.
A good riddance. Take the cats.

offer: Gammer Tuck is an old farmer with a long scythe and a longer grudge. He leads rebels who burn tax-collectors. He is usually drunk. He is also quite good with the scythe.
A rebel captain called Tuck. He is old, gruff, and heavily armed. He insists that the harvest belongs to the ones who sow it. The Cities disagree.
Tuck, the Plough Captain. A funny old man, if you ignore the corpses. Find him in the green edges and bring him in.
accepted: He keeps farmhands with him, more loyal than sensible. Do not underestimate them.
He roams the green country and the northern flats. He sings when he marches.
decline: I will not kill a farmer.
report: Tuck is gone? An old man's death. Still, the Cities are satisfied. Here is your payment.
The Plough Captain is dead. Good. The harvest is safe. Take the cats.
Done. An odd bounty, but a bounty. Your reward.

contracts.state: Sayo of the Grey Ribbon killed by player
offer: Sayo. The Grey Ribbon. A sand ninja who kills for hire. She leaves a ribbon on the body, and takes the coin from the corpse's pocket. We have eleven ribbons on file.
A cold professional is working the desert, called Sayo. She has killed three magistrates and a bard. The Cities want her stopped before she kills a fourth.
The Grey Ribbon. No one has seen her face and lived to describe it. Find her, kill her, bring the ribbon.
accepted: You will not find her. She will find you. Be ready for the quiet.
She works the desert and the canyons, and leaves no tracks. Watch the wind.
report: The Grey Ribbon is cut? Then my sleep will be easier. Here is your pay.
Sayo is dead. Good. Your reward.
A professional lost to a professional. Take the cats.

offer: Cuddy Pell. Mad as a flooded fish and twice as slippery. He claims the road is his dinner plate and he sets a place for every traveller. He carries a goat head in a sack. We do not ask.
A Mongrel loon called Cuddy Pell has been dining on the roads. Mostly he steals, sometimes he stabs, always he sings. Make it stop.
Pell. Small bounty, big noise. Wanders the wet country and the dry edges, talking to a sack. Rid us of him.
accepted: He is quicker than he looks. Do not trust a smile that wide.
Look near the floods and the mud pools. Follow the singing.
report: Cuddy is dead? I did not think him mortal. Here is your coin.
No more singing sacks. Good. Take your pay.
A small job, finished. Your reward.

contracts.state: Tchik of Seven Voices killed by player
offer: Tchik of Seven Voices. A Hiver drone who left the hive and took seven others with him. They speak as one, and they speak to you in seven different voices. Bring them down.
A rogue drone leads a hive-bandit pack through the dark fingers. Tchik, they call him. His troops are loyal to a point that frightens me.
Tchik. Cut loose from the swarm, he formed his own. No queen, no law. Only seven voices and a taste for travellers.
accept: A drone with a swarm. Understood.
accepted: His drones fight as one. Break one and the rest will break with it. Or kill them, worse.
He prowls the fingers and the desert near them. Listen for the clicking.
decline: I would rather not meet a swarm.
report: Tchik is gone? Seven voices, one scream. I am relieved. Here is your fee.
The swarm is broken. Good. Your payment.
A rogue drone, put down. A pity, perhaps. Take the cats.

offer: Elric Vosk was hired to guard a caravan. His employer cut his pay. He killed the master, the drivers and the pack-beasts, and kept the bell. Now he sells the road he once guarded.
A deserter of our own. Vosk. He stands at crossroads with a bell and offers escort. Those who accept are never seen again. The Guild is ashamed.
Vosk broke the first rule of the Guild: never kill the client. He killed nine. The Guild wants him dead and the contract voided.
accept: A killer guard. I'll do it.
accepted: He will meet you politely, as a guard would. He is expecting to be asked for work.
Look at the crossroads and the hills along the old desert tracks. The bell rings from afar.
decline: The Guild should clean its own house.
report: Vosk is dead? Then the Guild is clean again. Here is your fee.
The bell is silent. Good. Take your pay.
A hired blade, put down. A fair payment for a fair job.

offer: Pyke Ludlow was an Anti-Slaver. A true one. Then he decided that anyone who ever owned or traded a person deserved the same, and began killing them. Merchants. Farmers. A boy who sold a rope.
Ludlow. A freedom fighter gone sour. He kills anyone he finds who has ever bought a servant. The Cities would like a conversation with him.
An avenger named Ludlow works the roads. He leaves manacles on the dead, broken. A little too enthusiastic, the Anti-Slavers admit.
accepted: He is excellent in a fight and will not hear your side. Do not try.
He haunts the desert and flood roads where slavers once ran. Look for broken manacles.
decline: I side with him, a little.
report: Ludlow is dead. A sad end for a good man gone wrong. Take the Cities' coin.
The avenger is no more. Here is your pay.
A bitter bounty. Yours.

say: Orsa Quillon wants two cats a head and your cart's best wheel. Pay the first one fast.
She was a carter's wife once. Now she counts every wagon like it owes her husband.
The Toll-Widow's rope sits across the road past the Hub. Go around and you meet her friends.
Quillon never robs you. She only taxes you until you have nothing, then she stops.
My brother refused her toll. We found the cart.
Quillon is working the hills again, the woman with the rope. Drifters swear she hums while she does it.
Somebody on the Hub road killed a Shek courier for skipping the toll. Orsa Quillon's rope, they say.
A widow's rope and a dozen Dust Bandits who answer to her, and the Guild still won't send a proper escort.
Avoid the crest past the Hub after dusk. Quillon's lantern means the toll is open.
She taxes the poor, never the Guild's armoured wagons. Clever or cowardly, I can't tell.
There's a woman in the desert who charges road tolls with a rope and a grudge.
They say the Hub road has a widow on it who never lets a wagon pass free.
Quillon, I think. Some tollkeeper in the dust. Pay her or go around, whichever is longer.
A rope across the road and a lantern. That's all a traveller is told of her.
Toll, stranger. Everything you carry and I'll let you keep the boots.
Ah. Another wagon with no wagon. Pay what Edric would have asked.
Walk back or walk through me.
Edric stood here for twenty years for a few cats. I take what the road owes him.
You look like you can afford the road. Lift your hands and prove me wrong.
Toll paid. In full.
Good. The rope stays strung.
Edric would have let you go. I'm not Edric.
The rope is cut. Quillon is dead and someone has already hung a new one.
People say she fell with her lantern still lit. The road past the Hub is quiet for the first time in years.
Orsa Quillon finally paid a toll of her own. I only wish I had seen it.
A hundred wagons and not one mourner. Funny what a widow earns.
Quillon is in a cage. Imagine, being charged for the road she thought she owned.
They locked up the Toll-Widow. Her bandits scattered like dropped coin.
Somebody caught her alive. Rumour says she asks every guard for his toll through the bars.
Orsa Quillon caged, and the Hub road open. Brings a tear to a carter's eye.
Lord Dray accepts tribute, you understand. If you aren't offering it, he accepts it anyway.
He bows to everyone before he cuts them. Manners were the only thing his father paid for.
Ferrant Dray wears a signet ring that opens no doors anymore. He thinks it still does.
Heard him demand a bow from a farm girl at sword point. Then he took her mother's ploughshare.
The flats are Dray's court now. You'll know his hired men by the polished boots.
Some ruined noble is calling himself a lord of the northern flats. Wears a cape in this heat.
Dray, they call him. Titled, drunk on it, and quick with a blade.
A noble gone bad is worse than a bandit born. He knows how to be cruel politely.
Ferrant Dray was an Empire man once. Now he sells his own army's leftover insults.
Hired swords, a signet ring, and the manners of a gutted fish.
Somewhere north there's a lord with no land who robs travellers in full court dress.
They say a noble house collapsed and its third son took to the road. Dray, or Dreyne.
A cape, a sword, a title nobody honours. That's the gossip, anyway.
Imperial blood on the north road, charging fees.
Kneel, peasant. Or fall, if you prefer.
You stand in the presence of Lord Dray. Remove your hat. Then your purse.
My house was old and proud and it's dust. I shall make you dust too.
How tiresome. Another guest who hasn't brought a gift.
Dray doesn't beg, traveller. He collects.
Rise. No, remain kneeling. It suits you.
A modest win for the house of Dray.
Take notes, peasants. This is how a lord concludes a meeting.
Ferrant Dray is dead and his ring is missing. Somebody's wearing a dead house on their finger.
Lord Dray bled out in the flats like any peasant.
The fallen noble fell the last time. His hired swords went home to their mothers.
He died owing the Cities, the Guild and his tailor. In that order.
Lord Dray is in irons. They say he demands his meals be served on a tray.
The Cities have a nobleman in a cage. They say he complains about the draft.
Ferrant Dray, caged. It was always going to be either the sword or the stocks.
He claims diplomatic immunity from inside a cell. His guards enjoy it very much.
Hask Morrow is a Sentinel who stopped believing. He still takes the offerings, mind you.
I heard he wept when he first robbed a pilgrim. By the fifth, he did not.
The deserter in Okran's Pride keeps his Holy armour on. A mockery, or a habit.
Morrow sent a message to the Fist. It read: you left me hungry.
If you meet a Sentinel on the road with no patrol and no orders, it is Morrow.
A Holy deserter is preying on pilgrims. Good. Let them eat each other.
The Nation has a rotten Sentinel it can't catch. Funny how its holy fire misses.
Morrow, was it? Took his armour and his fear and went rogue.
Pilgrims come into the Cities with stories of a Sentinel who prays while he robs.
A deserter has the Holy army embarrassed. I buy a drink for whoever finds him.
Some Holy soldier lost his faith and now his purse is full. Typical priesthood.
I heard a deserter stalks the pilgrim roads in full Holy plate.
Morrow. A Sentinel gone off the rails. They say the Nation hasn't had a deserter before.
A Holy man who steals from the Holy. It's the oldest sin there is.
The Flame sees nothing here, traveller. Only me.
I swore an oath once. Look at me now. Yours is a small price.
Pilgrim or heathen, you pay all the same.
They fed me prayers. I want your food. Give it up, stranger.
Don't look at the armour. The man inside has left.
Say a prayer for me, whoever you worship.
Okran forgive me. Not that he has.
Another one down. The offerings add up.
Hask Morrow is dead. The Fist pretends it never knew him. The pilgrims are praying for him anyway.
The deserter fell in Okran's Pride. They buried the armour with him, the shame of it.
Morrow wanted a quiet death. Got a loud one.
The Nation sings of a good example. I sing of a hungry man put down.
Morrow is in chains, not in Holy ones. The Nation's furious that someone else got him.
A deserter in a cage, praying out loud. His captors do not interrupt him.
Hask Morrow caged. The Fist will want him back for a different kind of lesson.
They have the Sentinel. I hope the Holy Nation never gets him back, honestly.
Sarn Ashvael blesses you before he strips you. Swears it's for your own good.
They sing in the desert at dusk, hungry ones. You'll know it's him by the sermon.
The prophet of the Empty Bowl says every full belly is a theft. Mine is quite empty, but he doesn't believe it.
Fed a caravan crew to the sand and prayed over them.
He was a baker once, people say. The bread lie is the cruelest part.
A prophet of hunger is gathering mobs. No bowl will ever be full enough for him.
Sarn Ashvael, they call him. Walks the bone edge with a hundred hungry mouths behind him.
I saw his followers fight over a dead rat like it was communion.
He tells them the desert owes them, and the strong are the debt.
Starving men with a sermon are the worst kind of armed.
Some prophet is starving bandits into a cult. They say he never eats.
A starving preacher walks the east desert. Don't share your bread.
Ashvael, was it? A holy man for the hungry. He should have stayed holy.
Out in the dust a man blesses the hungry and they follow him into knives.
Brother, you're fed. Share the sin with me, and I forgive you.
The Empty Bowl calls. We answer by taking.
Look at us, stranger. We were people once. Your boots will remind us.
Feed us, and be blessed. Refuse us, and be fed to us.
Give what you carry and walk free.
The Bowl has been filled. Briefly.
Bless you, fallen one. You'll feed the faithful.
Eat, children. The desert provides.
The prophet of the Empty Bowl is dead. His mob won't stay a mob for long.
Sarn Ashvael, finally full of nothing. They buried him in the sand, half his followers fighting over the shovel.
I pity the hungry ones left. A prophet is easier to follow than to forget.
He preached about bowls until the blade came. May his be full.
Ashvael is caged. His followers wait outside the walls and sing.
They caught the prophet alive. He sermonises through the bars on the sin of waste.
Sarn Ashvael in chains. The mob hasn't scattered. It waits, and it's hungry.
A prophet in a cage still has an audience.
Veldt Harrow sits at the roadside with a book and a pen. You hope he's waiting for somebody else.
He taps the page twice for each prisoner. If he taps once, you weren't worth the ink.
The Tallyman bought a family and buried the grandmother alive to save the food. Marked it in the book, I heard.
I saw him once from far off. Writing. Always writing, never looking up.
Harrow keeps wet ground behind him. Whatever is out there, I won't look.
The Tallyman. That's what they call him now, the slaver who buries. Lord, I hope he never comes this way.
A slaver turned murderer is worse than both.
He still wears the old slaver coat, polished. The ledger never gets muddy.
Harrow's hunters never complain. I think they're afraid to.
Wet roads, a ledger, a pen. If you see them, go the other way.
There's a slaver who stopped trading and started counting. That's all I'll say.
Out in the flood country a man writes down the dead.
Some slaver killed his own market. They call him the Tallyman.
A butcher with a book. Nobody can tell me where the pages end.
Hold still, stranger. I'm trying to find your column in the book.
Another entry. Name, weight, use. Let's see what you fetch.
I sold a hundred souls once. Now I keep them.
You carry a lot of life for such a small purse.
Two taps for the keepers, one for the dead. Which will you be?
Mark him down. Another.
Two taps. Good.
Don't struggle. It ruins the handwriting.
The Tallyman is dead. They found a ledger, half burned, with more names than the Cities ever had.
Veldt Harrow bled on the same road he buried people on.
I hear the pen is still in his hand. No one wants to take it.
No more taps. The flood roads are very quiet tonight.
Harrow is caged. Every guard avoids his eyes, and he writes anyway.
They caught the Tallyman alive. He is asking for fresh paper.
Veldt Harrow under a lock. For the first time in years the ledger isn't in his lap.
He counts the bars now. He says there are always more than there should be.
Borun Vahl was the best of his circle, once. Now he is the thing mothers do not name.
The Oathless will not take your purse. Only your name and your life, in that order.
He cut the stone mark from his own arm and threw it at a priest's feet.
I saw Vahl in the canyons. He didn't draw. He didn't need to.
A flatskin asked him for passage and he gave it, and cut him down on the other side. His honour is a knife.
Some oathless Shek roams the dry mountains. He duels travellers for their boots and kills the winners.
Vahl, people say. The Kingdom won't discuss him.
A Shek with no mark and no master. A rare and dangerous creature.
Even other Berserkers keep their distance from Vahl. That's a high bar.
Borun Vahl keeps his scabbard empty. He draws from the air, so I hear.
A Shek exile hunts the canyons. It isn't a story I enjoy.
Some Shek lost his stone and now fights without rules. They call him the Oathless.
Vahl, I think. He doesn't take prisoners, nor coin.
A warrior without a creed in the mountains. Keep your blade sheathed and your mouth shut.
You wear no mark. Good. Then you have nothing to be ashamed of when you fall.
Draw, flatskin. I won't wait. I haven't waited since the circle.
The Golem judges me? Let him come. I'll judge you first.
I broke my oath so that I could be free. Free means you.
Another traveller, another stone to throw. Let the sand have you.
The sand takes another.
Honour is a weight. I put it down.
Be thankful. I don't usually let them kneel.
The Oathless is dead. Kral's kin are quiet. Even Shek who hated him say it was a clean death.
Borun Vahl fell in the stones. Somebody carved a mark on his arm afterward. Mercy, or insult, who knows.
He won't be named in the halls, but he will be remembered in the sand.
A broken oath, a clean blade.
Vahl is caged, and the Shek do not know whether to be ashamed or relieved.
The Oathless sits in a cell. Even the guards salute him, and then wonder why.
Borun Vahl alive in a cage. A Shek in chains is a terrible thing to watch.
They say he won't eat. He says only the free may break bread.
Ilsa Hearthmourn leaves candles at the edge of our fields. Nobody dares to touch them.
She was the hardest of the Pacifiers. Now she tells children the Flame is only fire.
Her voice is calm. That's the horror of it. The heretics are usually shouting.
A pilgrim told me he followed her out of the Pride for a day and a night. He hasn't spoken since.
People say she lights her candles from a flame no priest blessed.
A Holy apostate is spreading talk. I know that look. The Nation is afraid of a candle.
Ilsa something, a Pacifier who changed her mind. The Holy Nation has no humour about that.
I hear she sits with the pilgrims and tells them they are people, not tools. Dangerous words.
A candle in the dark and a woman who used to beat heresy out of men.
Hearthmourn, they call her. The faithful call her worse.
A Holy woman has turned against the Nation. They say she carries a candle. That's all I know.
Some apostate lights a candle at every camp. The Holy Nation won't say her name.
Hearthmourn. A good name for a heretic. A very bad one for a victim.
I heard a Holy killer woke up one morning and chose peace.
There's no Flame, stranger. Only a candle, and I have blown it out.
I was a hand of Okran once. Now I'm only a hand. Come closer.
Don't preach to me. I wrote the sermons.
Pray if you wish. It takes me longer to kill the praying.
You think me mad, or lost? I'm finally awake.
I'm sorry. I truly am. I am also not stopping.
The candle goes on. You don't.
Say whatever name you like. I'll hear it.
Ilsa Hearthmourn is dead and the Nation is lighting candles of its own. I don't know what that means.
They burned her candles after. The fields smell strange.
The Candle Heretic is gone. Her followers walk in circles looking for another.
An apostate in the dirt. The Nation sings.
Hearthmourn is caged. The Nation wants her back so very badly.
They have the Candle Heretic alive. Imagine the questions the Inquisitors have prepared.
Ilsa Hearthmourn is in a cell, and she's still lighting candles. Where does she get the wax?
She asked her guard if he was happy. He cannot sleep now.
Hodd Crake taught me to skin a bonedog. I won't be at the table when he eats.
The Long Appetite leaves clean bones. Neat, almost. Like he's being polite.
He still wears the Hunter's colours. It frightens the real ones more than the cannibals.
A hunter on a hunt will tell you the smell tells him. Crake says it tells him what to order.
We found his old camp. Three cooking pits, and a tally on the wall. Not cannibal marks. Hunter marks.
A Hunter gone bad, out on the bone plains. That breaks even a cannibal hunter's heart.
Crake. Used to be one of those bastards in the Bastion. Now he eats what they send.
A man who hunts cannibals and becomes one. Poetic, if you like cold poetry.
Carries a cleaver as long as my arm. It isn't for the hunting.
The Pride would pay to see him gone.
Some cannibal hunter turned sides. That's all anyone tells me.
A man called the Long Appetite is wandering the bone plains. Nobody wants to meet him.
I heard the Hunters lost one of their own to the thing they fought.
A hunter with a cleaver and a lonely smile, they said. Stay on the roads.
Easy, traveller. I only want a taste. A small taste.
I used to hunt things like me. Now I know what they were hungry for.
You smell of good living. I'll enjoy this.
Don't run. I hate chasing. It makes the meat tough.
A hunter never wastes a kill. I learned that early.
Thank you. I will eat in peace.
Clean kill. Such a waste if I didn't finish it.
Old habits. The best ones.
Hodd Crake is dead. The Hunters buried his colours separate from his body.
The Long Appetite fed the plains one last time. I won't mourn him.
I heard they found his tally on the wall, longer than any cannibal chief's. The Bastion burned it.
A hunter gone wrong, put down by a stranger. Perhaps that was the best way.
Crake is caged, and the Hunters can't decide whether to kill him or study him.
They have the Long Appetite alive. Don't feed him anything in front of him.
Hodd Crake in chains. He smiles at the guards. They stopped eating in front of him.
The Hunters want him dead, the Cities want him alive, and he wants dinner.
Pim Sillery steals a man's boots, then comes back for the laces. Unpleasant, but never lethal.
The Magpie leaves little glass beads where he lifted something. As a joke.
He lifted a power core from a sleeping Tech Hunter and sold it back to her for double. She was grateful.
Never leave anything shiny out near the Graveyard. The Magpie sees it from a mile away.
Sillery talks to himself as he steals. Argues with himself, actually.
There's a thief who steals only metal that glints. They call him the Magpie. Pim, is it?
He took a whole robot arm out of a ruin and swapped it for a dummy.
The Magpie is clever. That's what makes him dangerous. He knows the ruins like his own pockets.
I wouldn't hire him. Even for free. Not if he's the one counting.
A scrap thief out there with a dozen pockets and a taste for plans. The Hunters want him bad.
Some thief out west steals tech for fun. They call him the Magpie.
A Tech Hunter went rogue and now robs ruins. Quite the nuisance.
Heard of a scrap thief called Pim who steals more than he sells. Odd, that.
A man with a hundred pockets, the story goes. Nobody tells me why.
Ooh, shiny boots. Mine now. Mine, mine, mine.
Hello, traveller. You're about to lose something. I haven't decided what yet.
Give me your best gear and I might not take the rest. That's the Magpie's mercy.
I only steal from the dead and the dying. Which one are you?
Lovely buckle. Lovely teeth. I wonder which I'll take first.
Finders keepers. Ha!
Pockets full. Thank you, thank you.
Don't look so sad. Everything shiny eventually moves on.
The Magpie is dead. His nest was full of shining bits no one will claim.
Pim Sillery had a hundred pockets and every one was empty when they found him.
I heard his last act was to try to steal the knife that killed him.
No more stolen plans. The ruins feel safer already.
The Magpie is caged. They emptied his pockets and counted forty items. Nobody knows where thirty came from.
Pim Sillery behind bars. He has already stolen the guard's keys twice, they say.
They caught the Magpie, and the Hunters want their plans back. He claims he lost them. He didn't.
A thief in a cell. Let's see how long the lock lasts.
Teshin Ro doesn't shout. He only says your name, and asks if you'll draw.
The ronin cut down a Holy deserter at a well and drank from it afterward. Sat there until dusk.
He told me once that he lost his lord in a war nobody remembers. I believed him, and was sorry.
His sword is old. His coat is older. His habits are the oldest of all.
Ro leaves the dead sitting upright with their eyes closed.
A ronin walks the northern flats, challenging whoever he meets. The Cities fear him.
Ro, they call him. Teshin Ro. Worse than a bandit, because he's sorry afterwards.
I heard he cried at a funeral. His own victim's. He's that kind of man.
He bows before and after. Never in between.
A swordsman with no lord and no hurry. I almost wish him luck.
There's a ronin in the desert who duels every traveller. That's all anyone knows.
A masterless swordsman, so I hear. Even the Shek avoid him.
Teshin something. A man who fights because he forgot how to stop.
A ronin walks, a dead man follows. It is a story told at night.
You carry a sword. Draw it. I'd hate to cut an unarmed man.
My name is Teshin Ro. Remember it. It will be the last thing you learn.
I have no lord. No path. Only you, and the wind.
Bow, stranger. It's how it begins.
I take no coin. Only your answer to my question: will you draw?
Forgive me.
A good fight. Rest easy.
One more name to carry.
Teshin Ro has fallen. They say he was smiling at the end.
The ronin's sword is gone. Some say it was buried with him, others that it was sold. I hope it was buried.
Eleven men and one more. Ro settled his account at last.
The wind is calm over the northern flats. Strange how loud that is.
Ro is in a cell, and he refuses to eat until someone fights him fairly.
The ronin lets himself be caged. Says it's the only way to rest.
Teshin Ro in chains. He thanked his captors. They didn't know what to say.
A caged swordsman is a very quiet thing. The guards are afraid of the silence.
Ysolde Gorehollow has a laugh like a kettle. You hear it before the screaming.
Every raider in her nest wears a vial around the neck. Her blood.
I walked into her camp once to trade. The jars on the shelf were labelled by name.
She sings to the dead. They aren't interested.
Gorehollow has no army. She has a congregation.
A woman is bleeding travellers into jars out in the ashlands. They call her the Bloodmother.
Gorehollow, was it? Her raiders are getting bolder. Every month a caravan is short a crew.
She trades her jars to Skin Bandits.
The ashlands have always been hungry. Now they have a mother.
I heard her nest smells of iron. Not rust. Iron.
They say there is a mother in the ash who drinks the road dry.
A bloodraider matriarch. Nobody tells me which jar is whose.
Gorehollow is a name you'll know in a bad dream.
A woman and a jar collection. The ashlands aren't kind.
Come into the warm, little cup. Let me look at you.
How fresh you are! How full! How very generous of you.
Children, fetch the jars. Our guest has brought a gift.
I only take a little. At first.
Do not scream. It spoils the flavour.
Hang him. He'll drain nicely.
Lovely. Lovely. A full one.
Fetch the ladle.
The Bloodmother is dead. They're still breaking jars in the ash. Some of them weren't empty.
Gorehollow's laugh stopped. The ravens left the nest the same hour.
I hear her congregation sat in her camp for days afterward, waiting for her to come back.
The ashlands have lost their mother. They haven't lost their hunger.
The Bloodmother is caged. She asks the guards for their names.
Ysolde Gorehollow lives, in irons. Her raiders watch the walls and sing.
They caught her alive. I don't like how calm she is.
A mother in a cage. The ash is waiting.
Marta Cull measures the tide on her fingers. She knows how long a man holds his breath.
The Brine-Wife has a whistle. When you hear it, the Reavers come. It sounds like a gull.
She doesn't shout. She hums, and stands very still, and waits for you to move.
I lost a cousin to her tide line. She sent back his boots.
People say she was a salvager once. Then the sea took her husband and she took the sea's side.
A Reaver woman called the Brine-Wife is drowning crews on the south coast.
Cull has a way with a rope and a tide chart.
She ties them above the waterline and lets the sea decide.
The coast is dangerous enough. Now it has a hostess.
Reaver ships and Reaver dead. Cull has made it worse.
There's a woman on the south coast who drowns people on a schedule.
The Brine-Wife, they say. Terrible name, terrible woman.
A Reaver matron who counts tides. I'll never sail south.
Cull. A name the sea whispers, I'm told.
The tide is coming, traveller. Do you hear it?
Hold your breath. I want to see how long you can.
Salt on your lips already. That's the sea saying hello.
Come to the water. It's gentle.
You look dry. I'll fix that.
Tie him. Above the line. Slowly.
The sea will decide. It always does.
Good. Feed the water.
The Brine-Wife is dead. The tide has left her camp unwashed, which seems unfair.
Marta Cull drowned in the end, I heard. On dry land. How's that for sea justice?
No more gull whistle. The shore feels quieter and cleaner.
The south coast breathes again. A little.
Cull is caged, far from any water. She asks for a bucket and hums.
The Brine-Wife is in irons. Her Reavers wait in the surf.
They caught Marta Cull. The sea hasn't forgiven them.
A Reaver woman behind bars, and every guard checks the ceiling for leaks.
Teodric Clackjaw snaps his teeth when he thinks. Then he kills the thing he was thinking about.
He won't rob you until you've lost a fair fight. His fairness is an insult.
I saw him bow to a corpse before he looted it. Shell polished like a spoon.
He has a bell strapped to his back. Rings it to start. Rings it to end. There's no bell in between.
The crabbers follow him because he wins. That's the whole creed.
Some banned crab champion is running tournaments on the road. The prize is your life.
Clackjaw is the name. Don't ask him why he clacks. He has a very long answer.
He still thinks the pits are open. In a way, they are.
I heard his shell is made from the armour of eleven rivals.
A crab raider with a code is worse than a crab raider without.
There's a crab-pit champion loose in the south. I won't say his name; it clacks.
Out in the pits a fighter makes travellers duel.
A banned fighter with a shell. That's the whole of what I know.
Clackjaw. Sounds like a joke until you meet him.
Ring the bell! First round, stranger.
Clack, clack, clack. That is the sound of your luck running out.
Fair fight, they said. I'm the fairest killer you'll ever meet.
Show me your guard. No, higher. There. That's where I'll cut.
I was champion! Say it with me! Champion!
Round over. Winner stands. That's me.
The bell rings once. Always once.
A fair kill. Applaud, if you can.
Clackjaw is dead. They say you can still hear the clacking in the pits at night.
The champion lost the one fight he wasn't allowed to cheat in.
Teodric Clackjaw's shell ended up on a post.
The crabbers are fighting each other now. For the title, no less.
Clackjaw is in a cage and insists the match wasn't over. The guards have stopped arguing.
They caught the disgraced champion. He demands a rematch every dawn.
Teodric clacks his teeth against the bars. The sound is driving the prison mad.
A champion in chains. The crowd would pay to see it.
Maruka Tal-Khesh makes you stand in the sun while she counts. Reaching forty is a boast.
She says she walks Kral's last stand every day. She's the only one who thinks it's joyful.
A cut for every sin, she says. Then a cut for every virtue. In the end it's just cuts.
Her blade is chipped and her patience isn't.
I heard her laugh once, at the sixtieth.
The Hundred Cuts. A Shek woman of Kral's creed. Stay clear of the stone roads.
Kral's followers are mostly bluster. Maruka isn't bluster.
She has a tally scarred on her own arm. Every notch is a stranger.
She doesn't rob. She only measures.
A Chosen who takes the legend as a recipe. The Kingdom is ashamed.
Out in the Shek roads is a woman who counts to a hundred on the living.
A Kral zealot, they say. Her name is a long one.
The Hundred Cuts. Never ask her what happens at ninety-nine.
A Shek legend turned into a habit. A bad habit.
Weak flatskin! Stand. I'll count your breaths, and then your cuts.
Kral took a hundred and didn't kneel. You'll take one and beg.
Don't close your eyes. Counting is easier when you watch.
Your weakness offends the spirit of the stone. Let me cut it out.
One. There. You're already past most.
Ninety. Ninety-one. Ninety-two. Lie still.
Not quite a hundred. Not for lack of trying.
Kral approves. I don't.
The Hundred Cuts is dead. A hundred and one, they say, from the number of wounds.
Maruka fell in the stone roads. The Chosen buried her without a word.
She counted until the last. That's the part nobody wants to repeat.
The Kingdom has declared it a good death, which means it was a loud one.
Maruka is caged. She counts the bars out loud, over and over, until the guards weep.
The Hundred Cuts, alive and bound. The Kingdom asks to be told nothing.
She asked her jailer for a knife. He asked her why.
A Shek zealot behind bars. Some things shouldn't have lids.
Aldous Peel measures you with his eyes. Do not let him finish.
I know a man who met him and left in a better jacket. He didn't leave in the same skin.
The Tailor has a very polite way of speaking. Flat, like a floor. That's the worst of it.
They say he has a mirror in the ash, just so he can look at his coat.
A skin by the road is a signature. The Tailor doesn't sign twice.
Skin Bandits are a rumour to most. Peel is a name for those who have buried theirs.
I've never seen a man so careful with a knife.
Peel is a name from an old report. No one dares check it twice.
The ashlands don't lack monsters. Peel is one with a good tailor's eye.
A coat of skins. A hat of hair. I will not elaborate.
Out in the ashlands there's a tailor, they say, who works in skin. No one sends him orders.
A man in a coat of people. I don't tell this story twice.
Peel, the Tailor. A myth, they say. Myths don't leave scraps.
I heard the Skin Bandits have a name and a coat. I wish I hadn't.
You're well-proportioned. You'll fit the sleeves.
Stand still. The measuring is quick. It's the fitting that takes time.
Good skin. Clear, strong, fresh. I am pleased.
I won't hurt you more than is needed for the pattern.
Please remove your shirt. Or I will, afterward.
Excellent. The cut is straight.
Gather the thread. We have a new piece.
A fine fit. It will keep well.
The Tailor is unpicked. They say his coat was too heavy to burn, so they buried it.
They found Aldous Peel inside a coat of faces. It took three men to carry the coat out.
He came apart cleanly. Even the bandits clapped.
The ashlands are quieter, but I won't trust the quiet.
